nodes.name: Initiate Research Session
nodes.description: User can initiate a research session by entering a free-text research question.

nodes.name: Interprets User's Query
nodes.description: System interprets the user's query and produces a structured research brief (research question, hypotheses, scope constraints).

nodes.name: Engages Clarify Ambiguous
nodes.description: System engages with the user to clarify an ambiguous query, asking targeted questions until the research brief is sufficiently specific.

nodes.name: Generates Multiple Search
nodes.description: System generates multiple search query variants optimised for scholarly search APIs from the research brief.

nodes.name: Retrieves Paper Metadata
nodes.description: System retrieves paper metadata from scholarly sources using the generated queries.

nodes.name: Scores Retrieved Papers
nodes.description: System scores retrieved papers for relevance across multiple dimensions and produces a ranked list with accept/reject decisions based on configurable thresholds.

nodes.name: Specify Preferred Evidence
nodes.description: User can specify preferred evidence types in the research brief, and the system factors those preferences into paper ranking.

nodes.name: Tags Each Catalog
nodes.description: System tags each catalog entry with its evidence type for filtering and thematic grouping in the report.

nodes.name: Review Borderline-scored Papers
nodes.description: User can review borderline-scored papers and accept or reject them before download proceeds.

nodes.name: Downloads Full-text Content
nodes.description: System downloads full-text content for accepted papers from available sources.

nodes.name: Extracts Structured Findings
nodes.description: System extracts structured findings (claims, results, methodology, limitations) from downloaded papers into a research catalog.

nodes.name: Synthesises Research Catalog
nodes.description: System synthesises the research catalog into a structured report that directly addresses the original research question and hypotheses.

nodes.name: Persists Research Session
nodes.description: System persists research session artifacts (motivation brief, queries, ranked papers, catalog) to disk for later review or resumption.

nodes.name: List Previously Completed
nodes.description: User can list previously completed research sessions and open one for review.

nodes.name: Export Final Research
nodes.description: User can export the final research report as a PDF document.

nodes.name: Export Complete Research
nodes.description: User can export the complete research session (report + catalog + metadata) as an archive for sharing or backup.

nodes.name: Create
nodes.description: User can create, edit, and delete search queries before the search is executed.

nodes.name: Manually Upload Pdf
nodes.description: User can manually upload PDF papers to a research session at any time (before, during, or after search), creating Paper entries in 'approved' status.

nodes.name: Trigger Catalog Entry
nodes.description: User can trigger catalog entry creation for an approved paper that has content but hasn't been processed yet.

nodes.name: Edit Redact Extracted
nodes.description: User can edit or redact extracted findings in a catalog entry to correct or refine the system's output.

nodes.name: Import List Papers
nodes.description: User can import a list of papers from a citation management tool into a research session, producing Paper entries that the system ranks, downloads, and extracts into catalog entries.

nodes.name: Produces Sufficiency Verdict
nodes.description: System produces a sufficiency verdict after report synthesis - indicating whether the collected sources constitute an adequate review, and recommending action if not.

nodes.name: Produces Structured Hypothesis
nodes.description: System produces a structured hypothesis verdict in the report with a confidence assessment and links to supporting and contradicting sources.

nodes.name: Select One More
nodes.description: User can select one or more catalog entries and trigger 'find similar sources' — the system analyses selected papers' key findings, tags, and title to generate new targeted search queries.

nodes.name: Generates Citation Network
nodes.description: System generates citation network data (co-citation links between authors, citation links between papers) from the paper set for visualisation in the catalog view.

nodes.name: Groups Catalog Entries
nodes.description: System groups catalog entries by thematic agreement and produces a consensus summary showing the number of supporting sources per finding cluster.

nodes.name: Generate Citations Standard
nodes.description: User can generate citations in standard formats (BibTeX, APA, MLA, Chicago) for one or more selected papers and export them as a bibliography file.

nodes.name: Filter Search Papers
nodes.description: User can filter and search papers within a session by metadata fields (title, author, date, keyword) to locate specific papers in the collection.

nodes.name: Start Research Question
nodes.description: As a User, I want to start a session with my research question and receive a structured report answering it by the time the pipeline completes - including an evidence-type-tagged catalog, hypothesis verdict, and sufficiency assessment.

nodes.name: Upload Pdfs
nodes.description: As a User, I want to upload my own PDFs, trigger catalog extraction on demand, and edit extracted findings during or after a search so that I can enrich the session with sources the system didn't find or get wrong.

nodes.name: Access Share Past
nodes.description: As a User, I want to access and share my past research findings so that I can build on previous work and collaborate with others.

nodes.name: Import Curated Paper
nodes.description: As a User, I want to import my curated paper lists from a citation management tool into a session so that the system can rank, download, and extract findings for them alongside discovered sources.

nodes.name: See Citation Networks
nodes.description: As a User, I want to see citation networks and findings agreement clusters in the catalog so that I can identify key authors, seminal papers, and areas of consensus or controversy at a glance.

nodes.name: Percentage Completed Sessions
nodes.description: Percentage of completed sessions where the report directly addresses the research question and tests all stated hypotheses.

nodes.name: Percentage Catalog Entries
nodes.description: Percentage of catalog entries containing at least main claim, key results, and study design (non-empty fields).

nodes.name: Percentage Initiated Sessions
nodes.description: Percentage of initiated sessions that reach report generation (not abandoned mid-pipeline).

nodes.name: Percentage Sessions Sufficiency
nodes.description: Percentage of sessions where sufficiency check returns is_sufficient: true without needing rerun.

nodes.name: Percentage Sessions Stated
nodes.description: Percentage of sessions with a stated hypothesis that receive a non-null verdict in the report.

nodes.name: Percentage Sessions Clarification
nodes.description: Percentage of sessions where the clarification loop produces a research brief that the user confirms as accurate (user clicks 'proceed' without edits).

nodes.name: Percentage Generated Search
nodes.description: Percentage of generated search queries that return at least one paper metadata record from a scholarly source.

nodes.name: Percentage Retrieved Papers
nodes.description: Percentage of retrieved papers that receive a non-null relevance score and a valid accept/reject/threshold-band classification.

nodes.name: 100% Borderline-scored Papers
nodes.description: 100% of borderline-scored papers must be presented for accept/reject review before any download proceeds.

nodes.name: Percentage Accepted Papers
nodes.description: Percentage of accepted papers where full-text is successfully downloaded or flagged for manual upload.

nodes.name: 100% Catalog Entries
nodes.description: 100% of catalog entries must be editable and redactable by the user after extraction completes.

nodes.name: Time Seconds Display
nodes.description: Time in seconds to display filtered paper results after a metadata search query is submitted.

nodes.name: 100% Papers Imported
nodes.description: 100% of papers imported from a citation management tool must appear in the paper list with correct metadata (title, authors, date) within 60 seconds of import.

nodes.name: 100% Completed Sessions
nodes.description: 100% of completed sessions must be persisted to disk with all artifacts (brief, queries, papers, catalog) intact.

nodes.name: 100% Past Sessions
nodes.description: 100% of past sessions appear in the session list with correct metadata (title, date, status) when the list is displayed.

nodes.name: 100% Query Edits
nodes.description: 100% of query edits made before execution are saved and reflected in the next search batch.

nodes.name: Percentage 'export Pdf'
nodes.description: Percentage of 'export as PDF' operations that produce a valid, readable PDF file with all report sections.

nodes.name: 100% 'export Full
nodes.description: 100% of 'export full archive' operations produce an archive containing the report, catalog, and session metadata.

nodes.name: 100% Citation Export
nodes.description: 100% of citation export operations produce a bibliography file in the user-selected format with all selected papers.

nodes.name: Percentage 'find Similar
nodes.description: Percentage of 'find similar sources' results where the user accepts at least one suggested paper into the session.

nodes.name: 100% Catalog Entries
nodes.description: 100% of catalog entries with at least one co-author or co-citation relationship are included in the citation graph visualization.

nodes.name: Percentage Catalog Entries
nodes.description: Percentage of catalog entries that are assigned to a thematic agreement group at synthesis time.

nodes.name: ResearchSession
nodes.description: A named research investigation, identified by `session_id`. Contains a motivation brief, search tags, queries, papers, catalog entries, and report. Persisted as a set of JSON artifacts on disk.

nodes.name: KeyConcept
nodes.description: A term extracted from the research brief, carrying a context-specific `definition`, `synonyms` (feeds search tag generation), and `role` (construct, variable, method, outcome, or context).

nodes.name: SearchTag
nodes.description: A classification of terms derived from KeyConcepts. Three categories: primary_terms (strong relevance signal), supporting_terms (secondary signal), exclusion_terms (out-of-scope indicator). Also includes domain_tags, methodology_tags, and key_authors.

nodes.name: Query
nodes.description: A search string variant generated from SearchTags, carrying a formatted string, target endpoint, filters, execution order, and variant type classification (broad, narrow, methodological, author-focused, venue-focused, or temporal).

nodes.name: Search
nodes.description: A campaign within a research session, grouping queries and their collected scholarly documents. Manages the lifecycle of query execution, result collection, and document acquisition.

nodes.name: CatalogEntry
nodes.description: Structured findings extracted from an approved scholarly work. Contains bibliographic data, relevance score, extraction confidence, research alignment (hypothesis support/contradiction + evidence type), findings (main claim, key results, conclusions, limitations, future work), methodology (study design, sample size, dataset, methods/tools), evidence (key metrics with values, direct quotes), and related DOIs.

nodes.name: EvidenceType
nodes.description: Classification of a scholarly work's contribution type: empirical quantitative, empirical qualitative, systematic review, meta-analysis, theoretical, case study, or mixed. Used for filtering, tagging, and thematic grouping.

nodes.name: Report
nodes.description: The final synthesised output (defined by the output schema). Contains summary, hypothesis verdicts, and supporting evidence from catalog entries.

nodes.name: HypothesisVerdict
nodes.description: The report's assessment of the stated hypothesis: `supported`, `contradicted`, `mixed`, `insufficient_evidence`, or null (no hypothesis). Includes confidence score and supporting/contradicting DOI lists.

nodes.name: ExtractionFlag
nodes.description: Quality indicators on a structured finding when extraction is imperfect. Examples: short source, OCR noise, missing methods, paywall partial.

nodes.name: User
nodes.description: The human actor operating the Research Distillery system. Includes researchers, scholars, and graduate students conducting academic research.

nodes.name: System
nodes.description: The automated Research Distillery application that processes research queries, manages pipelines, and produces reports.

nodes.name: Session Manager
nodes.description: The system component responsible for creating, tracking, and persisting research sessions throughout their lifecycle.

nodes.name: Search Engine
nodes.description: The system component that executes queries against scholarly search APIs and retrieves paper metadata.

nodes.name: Ranking Engine
nodes.description: The system component that scores retrieved papers across multiple relevance dimensions and produces ranked lists with accept/reject decisions.

nodes.name: Downloader
nodes.description: The system component responsible for fetching full-text PDFs from open-access sources and Sci-Hub for accepted papers.

nodes.name: Document Processor
nodes.description: The system component that parses downloaded PDFs and extracts structured content for catalog entry generation.

nodes.name: Report Synthesiser
nodes.description: The system component that assembles the research catalog into a structured report with hypothesis verdicts and sufficiency assessments.

nodes.name: Persistence Layer
nodes.description: The system component that stores and retrieves all research session artifacts (briefs, queries, papers, catalogs, reports) on disk.

nodes.name: Citation Network Builder
nodes.description: The system component that generates co-citation and citation link data from the paper set for visualisation in the catalog view.

nodes.name: Citation Export
nodes.description: The system component that generates citation files in standard formats (BibTeX, APA, MLA, Chicago) for selected papers.

nodes.name: Error Handling Middleware (Shared)
nodes.description: The shared system component that intercepts failures across pipeline stages and presents actionable remediation options to the user.

nodes.name: ResearchBrief
nodes.description: Structured research brief derived from the user's free-text research question, containing hypotheses, scope constraints, and key concepts.

nodes.name: Finding
nodes.description: A structured piece of information extracted from a paper, containing a statement, supporting evidence, and optional confidence score.

nodes.name: Claim
nodes.description: An extracted assertion from a paper with supporting and contradicting evidence.

nodes.name: FindingCluster
nodes.description: A thematic grouping of catalog entries with a consensus summary showing supporting and contradicting source counts.

nodes.name: CitationNetwork
nodes.description: Citation network data containing co-citation links between authors and citation links between papers.

nodes.name: AuthorCoCitation
nodes.description: A co-citation link between two authors, recording how many times they are cited together.

nodes.name: ExportArchive
nodes.description: Metadata for an exported research session archive, including format, path, and included papers.

nodes.name: ClarificationTurn
nodes.description: A single clarification Q&A turn between user and system during research brief refinement.

nodes.name: UserEdit
nodes.description: A user edit or redaction to a catalog entry, recording the original and replaced values with timestamp.

nodes.name: VerdictOutcome
nodes.description: Possible outcomes for a hypothesis verdict: supported, contradicted, inconclusive, or not applicable.

nodes.name: SufficiencyVerdict
nodes.description: Assessment of whether collected sources constitute an adequate review.

nodes.name: Source
nodes.description: A scholarly document such as a paper, conference proceeding, preprint, or technical report. Identified by a unique identifier. May be retrieved via scholarly search APIs or imported from citation managers.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.description: A logged system event recording a failure with context (session, source, failure code) and suggested recovery actions.

nodes.name: SourceStatus
nodes.description: Lifecycle status of a source within a research session, from ranked through extracted or rejected.

nodes.name: CASE_CONTROL
nodes.description: An observational study where two groups are compared — one with the outcome of interest (cases) and one without (controls).

nodes.name: CASE_SERIES
nodes.description: A descriptive study tracking patients with a known exposure or treatment, without a control group.

nodes.name: SYSTEMATIC_REVIEW
nodes.description: A high-level study that identifies, appraises, and synthesizes all relevant studies on a research question.

nodes.name: CROSS_SECTIONAL
nodes.description: A study that observes a population at a single point in time to assess prevalence.

nodes.name: MIXED_METHODS
nodes.description: A study design that combines quantitative and qualitative research methods.

nodes.name: IN_VITRO
nodes.description: Research conducted in a controlled environment outside a living organism (e.g., cell culture).

nodes.name: IN_VIVO
nodes.description: Research conducted within a living organism (e.g., animal studies).

nodes.name: FORMULA_HEAVY
nodes.description: A PDF source that contains many mathematical formulas, which may have extraction errors.

nodes.name: SCANNED_PDF
nodes.description: A PDF that is a scanned image rather than text, potentially with poor OCR quality.

nodes.name: NON_ENGLISH
nodes.description: A source written in a language other than English, which may have translation gaps.

nodes.name: NOT_APPLICABLE
nodes.description: A verdict outcome indicating the hypothesis is not applicable to the collected evidence.

nodes.name: NEEDS_MORE
nodes.description: A sufficiency verdict indicating more sources are needed to reach adequate coverage.

nodes.name: AuthorCitation
nodes.description: A citation link between two authors, recording how many times they are cited together in the literature.

nodes.name: SourceCitation
nodes.description: A citation link between two scholarly sources, recording that one source cites another.

nodes.name: SessionSummary
nodes.description: A lightweight metadata snapshot of a research session, including title, status, and references to its queries, papers, catalog entries, and report.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.description: A single chat communication exchanged between the user and the system within a research session, carrying role (user/system), content, and timestamp.

nodes.name: Library
nodes.description: A curated collection of scholarly sources organized by the user, containing multiple research sessions and their associated papers, findings, and reports.

nodes.name: ErrorCode
nodes.description: Machine-readable error codes used to classify system failures, including network errors, parsing errors, download failures, rate limits, authentication failures, storage errors, validation errors, and unknown errors.

nodes.name: ErrorSeverity
nodes.description: Error severity levels used to prioritise error handling and user notification.

nodes.name: QueryStatus
nodes.description: Query execution lifecycle status, tracking a query from creation through execution to completion or failure.

nodes.name: QuerySource
nodes.description: Origin of a query: whether it was manually entered by the user, automatically generated from search tags, or derived from a similar source.

nodes.name: SearchStatus
nodes.description: Search campaign lifecycle status, tracking whether a search is currently running, has completed, or was cancelled.

nodes.name: ErrorRecovery
nodes.description: Suggested recovery actions for a logged error event, providing actionable remediation options to the user.

nodes.name: SessionFilter
nodes.description: Optional filter criteria used when querying research sessions, including status, text search, and library scope.

nodes.name: Hypothesis
nodes.description: A testable statement about the expected relationship between variables, derived from the research question and refined through the clarification process.

nodes.name: ResearchQuestion
nodes.description: The free-text question provided by the user that defines the scope and objective of the research session.

nodes.name: RelevanceScore
nodes.description: A numerical score computed by the ranking engine that indicates how well a paper matches the research question, used for accept/reject decisions.

nodes.name: Bibliography
nodes.description: A formatted list of citations for selected papers, exported in standard academic formats such as BibTeX, APA, MLA, or Chicago.

nodes.name: SessionState
nodes.description: The complete persisted state of a research session including all artifacts, ensuring zero data loss after transient failures.

nodes.name: CitationManager
nodes.description: A citation management tool (e.g., Zotero, Mendeley) from which users can import paper lists into a research session.

nodes.name: TransientFailure
nodes.description: A temporary failure in the pipeline (e.g., network timeout, API rate limit) that may resolve on retry without user intervention.

nodes.name: Consensus
nodes.description: The degree of agreement among catalog entries on a finding, measured by supporting versus contradicting source counts within a thematic cluster.

nodes.name: SourceMetadata
nodes.description: Bibliographic information about a scholarly source including title, authors, abstract, publication year, journal, and DOI, retrieved from search APIs.

nodes.name: AcceptRejectDecision
nodes.description: The user's explicit decision to include or exclude a borderline-scored paper from further processing.

nodes.name: Archive
nodes.description: A packaged export of a complete research session including report, catalog, and metadata, suitable for sharing or backup.

nodes.name: Authentication
nodes.description: The process of verifying the identity of a user or system component before granting access to resources.

nodes.name: Classification
nodes.description: The process of categorizing papers or findings into predefined categories or taxonomies.

nodes.name: Clustering
nodes.description: The unsupervised grouping of papers or findings based on similarity, used for thematic analysis.

nodes.name: Database
nodes.description: A structured data store (relational or document-based) used for persistent storage of application data.

nodes.name: Extraction
nodes.description: The process of extracting structured information (findings, claims, metadata) from unstructured PDF documents.

nodes.name: Filtering
nodes.description: The process of selecting a subset of items based on specified criteria.

nodes.name: Keyword
nodes.description: A significant word or phrase extracted from text, used for indexing and search.

nodes.name: Migration
nodes.description: The process of transferring data between storage systems, formats, or databases.

nodes.name: PDF
nodes.description: Portable Document Format, a file format used for distributing documents, commonly used for scholarly papers.

nodes.name: Parsing
nodes.description: The process of analyzing a string of symbols (text or structured data) to determine its grammatical structure.

nodes.name: Ranking
nodes.description: The process of ordering papers or results by relevance score or other criteria.

nodes.name: Retry
nodes.description: The act of attempting an operation again after a failure, often with exponential backoff.

nodes.name: Scoring
nodes.description: The process of assigning a numerical value to indicate quality, relevance, or confidence.

nodes.name: Schema
nodes.description: A blueprint or definition of the structure of data, including field names, types, and constraints.

nodes.name: Version
nodes.description: A specific release or iteration of a software component, document, or data model.

nodes.name: Parallel Paths (feed into pipeline at any point)
Must Implemented Dynamically
nodes.description: System must be implemented with a dynamically typed language suitable for data processing and a browser-based Web UI.

nodes.name: All Session Artifacts
nodes.description: All session artifacts must be stored as on-disk JSON files with raw PDFs — no database dependency.

nodes.name: Support Pdf Structural
nodes.description: The system must support PDF structural extraction with ≥90% completeness using Docling.

nodes.name: Operate Single-user
nodes.description: The system must operate as a single-user, single-session application with no multi-tenant authentication.

nodes.name: Each Paper Must
nodes.description: Each Paper must have a unique DOI within a session; papers without DOI are excluded from automated pipeline.

nodes.name: One Catalogentry Exist
nodes.description: Only one CatalogEntry may exist per Paper (1:1 relationship).

nodes.name: Handle Sci-hub Dns
nodes.description: The system must handle Sci-Hub DNS failures gracefully with user prompts for manual upload.

nodes.name: All Persisted Json
nodes.description: All persisted JSON artifacts must carry a schema_version field with migration support.

nodes.name: Report Generated
nodes.description: Once a report is generated, the pipeline is terminal; updates require explicit re-synthesis.

nodes.name: Search Execution Must
nodes.description: Search execution must complete within ≤5 minutes per query variant across all endpoints.

nodes.name: Paper Scoring Must
nodes.description: Paper scoring must complete within <10 seconds per batch.

nodes.name: Storage Budget Must
nodes.description: Storage budget must not exceed 200 MB per 30-paper session.

nodes.name: Session State Must
nodes.description: Session state must be preserved with 100% artifact integrity after transient failures.

nodes.name: Manual PDF Upload and Findings Editing
New Research Session
nodes.description: A new research session can be started in 2 or fewer interactions (type query, press Start).

nodes.name: Borderline Paper Review
nodes.description: Borderline paper review displays title, abstract snippet, and relevance score on the list view without requiring the user to open the detail panel.

nodes.name: Any Point Pipeline
nodes.description: At any point in the pipeline, the user can determine the current stage from tab indicators and status icons without ambiguity.

nodes.name: Download Extraction Fails
nodes.description: When a download or extraction fails, the user is presented with at least two actionable options (e.g., Retry, Upload Replacement, Exclude) within 2 seconds.

nodes.name: Paper Catalog Tables
nodes.description: Paper and catalog tables support sorting by at least 3 columns, display in compact density, and load the first 20 rows within 1 second.

nodes.name: Minimize cognitive load during borderline paper review
Provide transparent system state at every pipeline stage
Provide clear remediation paths on failure
